d126-mixed-observation.json is the literal source substring from the opening
brace through the matching closing brace of the selected report. No JSON
re-encoding, indentation changes, identity substitution or timestamp changes.
The source is a captured report_payload value; it does not establish the
original agent HTTP body's whitespace. The HTTP regression sends these exact
fixture bytes, bypassing the usual test helper's JSON marshaling.

The unit proof pins the fixture hash and checks complete JCS-byte equality
through typed serialization. The integration proof checks both entrypoints,
JSONB value equality and complete JCS-byte/hash equality after storage. PostgreSQL
report_payload is JSONB, so this is not a claim of literal wire-byte retention.

The checks and recent_errors exposed by NodeDetail retain their original
arrays, timestamps, messages and codes. Operation projections expose their own
step/final codes; they do not expose observation arrays. Current NodeDetail has
no forwarding_block_reasons field. The report's reasons remain intact in its
stored payload. Neither an accepted receipt nor the reported generation alone
is an applied-policy ACK or permission to publish (§5.1, §5.2, §14.4–§14.5).
